preview_text: Winter is always a time to nail down some quality hours of training, without the distraction that competition can sometimes bring. When we, as a squad, were figuring out what to do over Winter 2022/23, we received an invitation that we couldn’t turn down from the Australian Sailing Team.
rich_text:
Winter is always a time to nail down some quality hours of training, without the distraction that competition can sometimes bring. When we, as a squad, were figuring out what to do over Winter 2022/23, we received an invitation that we couldn’t turn down from the Australian Sailing Team. Having a high quality training group is imperative and we didn’t need much convincing for a trip down under to train against some of the best in the world. 
So, just after Christmas and over the last few days of 2022, we headed off to AUS - albeit I had a bit of a longer trip via the US to save 30% on my airfare.

![1](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/1_1eb3149069.jpeg)

![2](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/2_0b5bceba59.jpeg)

I arrived at our first stop in Sydney, settled in and quickly got on the water ready for the Australian Nationals. Unfortunately a few days were cancelled due to bad weather, but it did allow us to explore Sydney. Sailing-wise I was suffering a little from a few little niggles and finished up 9th overall.

![3](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/3_037d626d90.jpeg)

![4](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/4_6feb5b3320.jpeg)

![5](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/5_2a91ff206c.jpeg)

![6](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/6_6906fd0605.jpeg)

After two weeks in Sydney we moved onto Melbourne, where we all competed at SailMelbourne in what turned out to be another windy week. I finished up 6th overall there.

![7](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/7_42b9e071d6.jpeg)

![8](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/8_2897877181.jpeg)

![9](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/9_659e99c5ec.jpeg)

Another couple of weeks there and it was time for our final stop, Adelaide. We were based in Adeliade for almost a month this time, getting used to the venue where our ILCA world championships will be in 2024. We had a proper mix of conditions here, including some absolutely massive days. Great fun.

![10](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/10_5006a2eb43.jpeg)

Below: Enjoying the last few days of Australia with a sunset and a helicopter ride down the coast.

![11](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/11_14fa852fb7.jpeg)

![12](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/12_4548bbfe6a.jpeg)

After nearly two months abroad and some quality hours on the water it was finally time to head back home to the UK. Having been in aussie summer for some time it was a bit of a shock coming back to the UK temperatures. Still feeling cold two weeks on!

Last weekend I found some time to head up to the RYA Dinghy & Watersports Show, which is always good fun. Great to see many friends from across the water sports world and I even did a ILCA speed talk with Hannah Snellgrove, which seemed to go down well.

*(Below: photo credits Will Carson RYA BST)*

![13](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/13_03f528e914.jpeg)

![14](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/14_1701ba98c9.jpeg)

Returning back to Weymouth, attention quickly turned to preparing my boat and equipment for the European regatta season. That meant getting new sails, masts, booms, the lot and led to some interesting logistical challenges, as you can see in this photo here....

![13](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/13_57c040bbbb.jpeg)

I also redesigned my compass/watch mount that I built with Actisense in 2019/2020. It has been great over the past 4 years but the time had come to redesign her and make her smaller and lighter. Pleased to say this new model is much stronger, smaller and has a 62% reduction in weight. Cheers to LJ Furniture and Shock Sailing for all the help in making this go from a drawing to reality in less than a week.

![14](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/14_3bde59934a.jpeg)

And finally this weekend just gone by I headed to Stokes Bay SC for the first UKLA Qualifier of the year. We had an exceptionally difficult light and tricky weekend but pleased to say I managed to come away with the win. Full results here: [www.sailwave.com/results/ukla/qualifiers/230304_Stokes_Bay_Q1](https://www.sailwave.com/results/ukla/qualifiers/230304_Stokes_Bay_Q1.htm)
Huge thanks to Duncan from SailingFast for sorting me out with basically a complete boat on the morning of the first race as all my kit was in Europe.

*(Below photo: [Lotte Johnson](https://www.instagram.com/saillotts/))*
![15](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/15_4b9d851247.jpeg)

Next up: Princess Sofia regatta at the end of March!

Cheers,

Sam

preview_text: It has been a chock-a-block couple of months, with one of the biggest years of the sailing calendar kicking off. Here's how things have panned out for me.
rich_text:
Hi everyone,

It has been a chock-a-block couple of months, with one of the biggest years of the sailing calendar kicking off. Here's how things have panned out for me.

Mid-March was all about Palma and more specifically the build up to the prestigious Princess Sofia Regatta. We did a fitness/sailing camp beforehand and managed to fit a Sa Calobra ascent on the final day.

![1](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/1_47a0631e93.jpeg)

Next job was to get my boat, sail, equipment and kit all race ready.

![2](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/2_58ab58e829.jpeg)

Every year over 1000 sailors across all the Olympic classes descend on Palma and this year the competition was as tight as always.

![3](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/3_10decb8663.jpeg)

It was a light and slow start of the regatta with a bit of patience required. I had a solid start in one abandoned race but found my performance through the week quite inconsistent, something that has been quite rare for me over the past year. In the end I finished 23rd overall out of 184 boats, a solid result but one I was slightly disappointed with. 

![6](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/6_a40a18f144.jpeg)

The story was similar in Hyeres, I had some moments and I *had* some moments. Struggled to piece together a consistent story around the race track and it showed in my results, as I finished 25th overall. 

![4](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/4_b204048fd2.jpeg)

Sport is weird sometimes; you can prepare for months on end, put so much energy into perfecting every detail -and yet still sometimes it doesn’t quite come together when you want it. 
In hindsight, in the effort to improve last winter, I was so fixed about de-constructing my sailing I think I lost my processes in my normally super-strength conditions, which in turn had a knock on effect and meant I was struggling to rely on skills that had delivered in the past. 

The important thing is that there were some brilliant, shining lights in my performance compared to last year and I was very happy with how these areas of my sailing had progressed. It's one of those where yes, I'm not happy with how I've performed, but I know if I keep on trucking and pushing forwards, another breakthrough will happen. Plus, 23rd and 25th on a bad day is still a bloody good result in the grand scheme of things.

![5](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/5_5dcdb6f425.jpeg)

After a busy 6 months in the ILCA/Laser world it was nice to get back to Weymouth and let my hair down a bit. I had a couple of weeks off, filled with plenty of gym, fitness and sailing other boats.

![7](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/7_98c7258592.jpeg)

![8](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/8_01183f30e6.jpeg)

The Musto Skiff was also a blast, learning to trapeze and use a spinnaker for the first time. Awesome fleet too and great fun racing at the WPNSA Skiff Open.

![9](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/9_90fa278abd.jpeg)

I then set out on a bit of an adventure I've wanted to do for years, sail around Portland in the WASZP. 
Launching at 8:30am in a stiff north easterly breeze, I sent it around the island and rounded the channel mark on the other side of Chesil Beach after just one hour. Rather crushingly, on the return journey the wind shut down so there was a bit of low riding and eventually I got my support rib to give me a tow for the final few miles. To be honest that was a bit gutting, as I now feel like I haven't properly completed the challenge yet! I reckon a sub-2 hour circumnavigation certainly is possible in a WASZP so for sure, one day I will be back.

**Current record: 2 hours 52 minutes (with tow). 27.7 nautical miles sailed.**

preview_text: What a year it has been. Highs and lows are a normal part of life as an athlete and this year has been no exception. This years world championships, in The Hague, Netherlands, were full of both.
rich_text:
What a year it has been. Highs and lows are a normal part of life as an athlete and this year has been no exception. This years world championships, in The Hague, Netherlands, were full of both highs and lows for many eventful reasons - as you will soon find out!

The drama started when my pre-event preparations back home got off to a rocky start after l managed to catch COVID just days before I was meant to leave. This subsequently delayed my arrival into the Netherlands and meant, upon arrival, I was already foot on the accelerator getting myself into competition mode. I quickly set about getting stuck into training and adjusting to the tidal and wavy conditions and before I knew it the event got underway. Spread over 8 days, these worlds really were a war of attrition. 

![9](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/9_4c0eacabbf.jpeg)

After a strong start on day one, I had a small wobble on day two but safely made it through into gold fleet racing. Sadly, this was also the day that someone decided to steal my bike, hence the chaotic nature of this event! (I've never recovered it - if you see a bike like this let me know!)

![2](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/2_791684df71.jpeg)

Anyway back to the sailing.

![10](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/10_2788cbed01.jpeg)

Gold fleet can be a brutal place sometimes and the rest of my week was a series of up and downs. I think the two photos below sum up this entire year pretty well - one moment winning and leading races and then something happens. 

![11](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/11_c06fba2861.jpeg)

![12](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/12_5bb2781f46.jpeg)

Despite the difficult circumstances surrounding the whole week, probably the highlight was winning the very final race of the championship. I came off the pin end, had good speed to lead at the first windward and then had a solid first downwind to wrap up the race. 

![13](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/13_f186ac14af.jpeg)

Overall, I finished 36th out of 140 competitors. Worse than last year, sure, but sometimes you've got to go backwards in order to take a bigger step forwards. I am very much looking forward to solving this over the coming months and into 2024.

_______________________________________________________________________________

preview_text: After a bit of time off post-worlds I got myself back into Weymouth and got back on the bike again. Strength and fitness quickly turned into the goal from September onwards and together with fellow squad members Micky, Elliot and JPC, we all got ourselves mountain bikes.
rich_text:
After a bit of time off post-worlds I got myself back into Weymouth and got back on the bike again. On reflection, I spent a large part of this year at a lighter weight than I believe optimum for the boat, so naturally strength and fitness quickly turned into the priority from September onwards. The entire Weymo squad consisting of Micky, Elliot, JPC and myself all got ourselves mountain bikes (well actually I bought another one from ebay for £345 after my previous MTB was stolen at the Worlds - see previous blog post 😢😡) and started putting in some serious hours along various routes around the Jurassic coastline.

Mountain biking is a fun deviation from our traditionally road bike orientated program. With some brilliant routes around Weymouth & Portland it seemed like a great way to get out and put some hours in without things becoming a bit too mundane. Micky did, however, find out the hard way that even mountain bikes don’t work on Chesil Beach…

![2](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/2_0b340c5aa1.jpeg)

![3](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/3_2b08a259db.jpeg)

In between my training I spent a day at the Southampton Boat Show, doing a talk about professional sailing on the Foredeck Stage. It was a great day out, as always, especially going with friends. 

![3.5](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/3.5_0f34391d17.jpeg)

Next up was my first Moth Nationals. I travelled down to Plymouth after only a few days in the boat and managed to smash out a 6th place finish overall. Great day and great racing.

![4](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/4_5ee013ebc6.jpeg)

Followed by more mountain biking back home…

![5](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/5_35beb1a50a.jpeg)

Next up was the Endeavour Trophy in Essex. This champions of Champions regatta is where every national champion competes in one design boats against each other. After winning the WASZP nationals in June I had earnt my ticket to the prestigious event, however needed to find a crew and a boat. Up stepped in Larissa Connabeer, a 200 sailor who also had a pristine boat. Ideal.

![6](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/6_b55c7a9021.jpeg)

We were a touch underweight for the windier races but managed to find our grove towards the end of the day and were up there fighting at the front.

![7](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/7_0ca97fea62.jpeg)

.... And we ended up finishing 5th overall! Not bad for less than an hour in a 200 since the last Endeavour I did in 2019.

![8](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/8_e87127d8ac.jpeg)

![9](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/9_f3ada598df.jpeg)

Flying out straight from the Endeavour I headed out to Cadiz, Spain, to help out with the WASZP program at the SailGP event.

![10](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/10_ee88a394e2.jpeg)

It was a pretty cool week seeing the boats up close and even meeting F1 driver Seb Vettel.

![11](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/11_10ebfb0c67.jpeg)

![12](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/12_248a36ff8f.jpeg)

![13](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/13_60468ad9a1.jpeg)

After a busy week in Cadiz, I was looking forward to getting back to Weymouth and settling into a big block back in the boat, mixed in with a few qualifiers. 

![14](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/14_7a91a1d8db.jpeg)

The first Autumn qualifier was in Paignton and after some light and funky conditions I finished up 2nd to Micky. Full results here: **[https://www.sailwave.com/results/ukla/Qualifiers/2023_Q4_Paignton.htm](https://www.sailwave.com/results/ukla/Qualifiers/2023_Q4_Paignton.htm)**
![15](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/15_e4383983fa.jpeg)

The last autumn qualifier was at WPNSA and I had a proper battle with Micky all weekend. These fantastic photos were taken by Optical Marine **(https://www.opticalmarine.com/)**.
Full results here: **[https://www.sailwave.com/results/ukla/qualifiers/231021_WPNSA_Q6_ILCA_7.htm](https://www.sailwave.com/results/ukla/qualifiers/231021_WPNSA_Q6_ILCA_7.htm)**

![16](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/16_e2ac9a3021.jpeg)

Cheers Ovington for the rocket boat and Optical Marine for the photos.

![17](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/17_39a2140f04.jpeg)

The big news regarding Olympic selection happened at the start of October, where teammate Micky Beckett officially got selected for the Paris 2024 Olympics next year. He has been sailing phenomenally for the past two years and rightfully so is a clear favourite to medal. Obviously, I would have loved to have been selected myself, but the sheer consistency Micky has shown has meant he is the best bet at hopefully bringing back a medal for GB next year. 

My job now switches into a training partner role, helping and challenging Micky daily to ideally make winning a medal inevitable. Hopefully, I can learn from him and progress my sailing forwards at the same time, just like what he did with Elliot Hanson in the previous Tokyo Olympics cycle.

![0.5](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/0.5_d18b1d4d6c.jpeg)

You can follow Micky and his build up to the Olympics in August next year on his page here: **[instagram.com/mickybeckett/](https://www.instagram.com/mickybeckett/)**

____________________________________________________________________

Back to my sailing. I jumped back in the WASZP, for the first time since the nationals in June, for the End of Season Championships at Rutland. It was a light and shifty affair with plenty going on, even without the added complication of fancy dress we were all wearing on the Saturday of racing. Can you tell it was Halloween?

![18](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/18_7bce75a569.jpeg)

![19](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/19_21248a0ec8.jpeg)

![20](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/20_ce8cb105ae.jpeg)

![21](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/21_d40e6ac8a3.jpeg)

With some very close competition from Ross Banham and Hattie Rogers I managed to win the event and seal off a great WASZP year. Hopefully I’ll be at the WASZP worlds next year…

![23](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/23_c9bb44d57a.jpeg)

Back to work in the ILCA and another Weymouth - Swanage downwinder complete. 

![24](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/24_958763a1fd.jpeg)

Followed by some more MTB around Portland…

![25](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/25_9472b4dca1.jpeg)

Early December and Vilamoura (Portugal) calls. Just last week we completed one very productive training camp, albeit in slightly lighter winds than what might be ideal for our World Championships – which are in Adelaide, Australia, just over a month away.

![26](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/26_28571dced6.jpeg)

![27](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/27_947e809655.jpeg)

In other news I have also listed my carbon aerovanes for sale on the INGEN Sailing website. Check them out here if you’d like to buy one: **[INGEN Sailing Carbon Aerovane](https://ingensailing.com/products/e2w2xxg5rf2pzkxozolkobeva3mco0)**

![28](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/28_2d605ef569.jpeg)

What next? I’m lucky to be spending Christmas at home before flying out to Adelaide, Australia, for New Years. The plan is to spend a month there racing and training and preparing for my biggest event of 2024, the ILCA 7 World Championships at the end of January. Looking forward to it already.

Cheers for all the support!

**Sam**

rich_text:
Hello blog. Long time no see!

Been a while since I found the time to sit down and write about the past six months. With Micky being selected for the Olympics late last year, my focus has shifted into more of a training partner role, where I want to soak up as much knowledge as possible and help push him to win a gold at this year's Olympic Games.

September – November 2023 was a brilliant building fitness block, with many hours under my belt on the bike and in the gym back home in Weymouth. Coupled with a few Vilamoura training camps leading up to December made it a very productive period and I had a half-decent regatta to finish off the year at the Vilamoura GP, ending up 6th overall.

rich_text:
After a short break back home for Christmas, it was back on the road again. This time going back  down under to Adelaide, Australia, in preparation for the big event of my year; the ILCA World Championships 2024. 

![7](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/7_c6f0441843.jpeg)

From numbering up sails at 5am whilst jet lagged on day one, to laminating carbon onto my tiller in the build up to the practice event, it was a fruitful training block in the lead up to the worlds.

Our charter boats lined up ready to go:

![19](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/19_6a57be69d3.jpeg)

![14](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/14_ead1cdd976.jpeg)

The worlds was quite a mixed bag. Some good results mixed up with some shockers had me yo-yoing up and down the leaderboard, but in the end I finished a respectable 18th overall out of near 200 competitors. 

![20](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/20_76163d1123.jpeg)

![16](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/16_f27fb80681.jpeg)

18th is a solid result but naturally I would prefer much more. The positive is that this year is I saw some big changes in my sailing, especially in my speed off the wind, which gives me a lot of confidence that I'm moving forwards on the right path.
 
Some holiday snaps:

![9](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/9_af2d57c6fa.jpeg)

![18](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/18_1b780c7eb7.jpeg)

![2023 SWS SLIM LONG](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/2023_SWS_SLIM_LONG_9a113af3c0.png)
title: ILCA Worlds AUSTRALIA

Heading back from Australia, it was time to take a little break from training and switch off for a couple of weeks to do some different activities. 

![26](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/26_3dc3546ef9.jpeg)

I rigged up the WASZP for the first time in three months and set about remembering how to foil. Next took a small trip up to Farmoor Reservoir with the WASZP mid-February to compete at the Oxford Blue, a Sailjuice winter series event. It was a good experiment with the WASZP handicap, which I think maybe needs revising a little bit more before we can race competitively against everyone else.

![farmoor](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/farmoor_3843f12db7.jpeg)

Farmoor was also one of the first events I went to when I started sailing back in 2010, so it was great to be back and race against Rob Howlett, one of my original coaches from back in the day. Fair to say we have changed a bit since then.

![27](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/27_17cfa4715d.jpeg)

![28](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/28_bf278bcbe7.jpeg)

Heading back to Weymouth I got back on the water doing some surfing with Jack.

![29](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/29_bb1d432680.jpeg)

A few cold WASZP sessions!

![30](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/30_b53ac0772c.jpeg)

And finished off the mini-break with the Dinghy Show in Farnborough.

![31](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/31_218d906b59.jpeg)

Next up: Back in the ILCA in Palma for some training and the build up to Princess Sofia Regatta.

Long time no speak. Just over a year has flown by and I am slightly behind with my goal of doing one blog post a month 😂

It's been a tricky year which firstly started off with the build up to the Paris 2024 Olympics and my role in supporting Micky in his quest for an Olympic Gold medal. It was intense, rewarding but ultimately ended up fruitless when the Olympics didn't quite go Micky's way and he missed out on a medal.

Starting off in Palma we had a stunning day for an Ovington photo shoot:

![1](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/1_f28b8abde1.jpeg)

![2](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/2_9553bf578a.jpeg)

![3](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/3_f1301040d7.jpeg)

![4](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/4_b26c382575.jpeg)

![5](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/5_e26808740d.jpeg)

![7](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/7_90f1547dc5.jpeg)

The regatta itself was a mixed bag for myself. Faster, fitter but a few bad calls left me 19th overall.

Fair to say it was pretty packed in our van.

![6](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/6_7261d4b877.jpeg)

![9](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/9_5348b06dd1.jpeg)

![10.5](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/10.5_6292e2d2fb.jpeg)

Moving onto Hyeres and I bet Dimitri I couldn't put all my sail numbers, GBRs, stickers and flags on within 30 minutes. 24 minutes later:

![10](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/10_09b9084fa5.jpeg)

The regatta started off well with a 4th but sadly that night I got badly ill and was bed bound for a couple of days. Ah well.

![11](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/11_03ae5dee18.jpeg)

Next up we moved to Garda for bit of a fitness/speed camp.

![12](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/12_bd68fea905.jpeg)

![13](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/13_e3da392436.jpeg)

![14](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/14_a77f4f2516.jpeg)

After Garda I was starting to ramp up my WASZP sailing again, ready for the worlds in August. I stopped off at Lake Como on the way home, a really stunning place, and rented a WASZP for a couple of days.

![15](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/15_17b5a35ffc.jpeg)

![16](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/16_20bfb5284f.jpeg)

Back to the UK and I was lucky enough to be invited to Goodwood Festival of Speed by Polestar. Even went up the iconic hill climb in the Polestar 2. Insane speed And a great day out.

![17](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/17_28d2ac427f.jpeg)

![18](https://admin.samwhaley.com/uploads/18_a774d37dfd.jpeg)

Thanks Polestar.
